title: Annotatio IV §.XVIII open: From Gaul Waldenses — English Waldenses / Wycliffites (Age XIV)
pass_a_gloss: §. XVIII. From the Waldenses so called kat' exochēn — i.e. born in Gaul in the XIIth Age and propagated in the XIIIth — the ENGLISH WALDENSES drew their origin in the XIVth AGE, called by one name Wycliffites from John Wycliffe, English Doctor, who flourished in the Year 1370. His Theses opposed both to Transubstantiation and to Consubstantiation Franciscus Foris Otrokocsi collected in the Irenicum pp. 57 and 58, partly from the Council of Constance in which they were condemned, partly from Book IV of the Trialog chapters 7 and 43 On the Lord’s Sermon on the Mount.
pass_b_english: §.XVIII: from the Waldenses so called par excellence — born in Gaul in Age XII, spread in XIII — came the ENGLISH WALDENSES of Age XIV.
One name: Wycliffites, from John Wycliffe (English doctor, ~1370). Otrokocsi gathers his theses against both Transubstantiation and Consubstantiation from Constance (where condemned) and the Trialog.
source_text: §. XVIII. A Waldensibus kat' exochēn sic dictis, i.e. in Gallia Seculo XII. natis, & XIII. propagatis, originem traxere WALDENSES ANGLI, SECULO XIV, unô nomine WICLEPHISTÆ dicti à Johanne Wiclepho, Doctore Anglo, qui floruit Anno 1370. Hujus Theses, tum Transsubstantiationi, tum Consubstantiationi oppositas, partim ex Concilio Constantiensi, in quo damnatæ sunt, partim ex IV. libro Trialog. cap. 7. & 43. de Sermone Domini in monte, collegit Franciscus Foris Otrokocsi in Irenico p. 57. & 58.
